news.title: Broccoli AI, which sells AI agents to plumbing, HVAC, and electrical companies, raised a $22M Series A and a $30M Series B; a source says it is valued at $300M (Nick Lichtenberg/Fortune)
news.title_en: Broccoli AI, which sells AI agents to plumbing, HVAC, and electrical companies, raised a $22M Series A and a $30M Series B; a source says it is valued at $300M (Nick Lichtenberg/Fortune)
news.author: Fortune
news.article_content:
When Marcelle Flowers’ staff told her that two students were waiting at the counter of her Sacramento plumbing shop, she grabbed her wallet. She assumed they were selling chocolate bars for a soccer team.

“I literally said, you have five minutes,” recalled Flowers, now 62 years old. It was June 2024, and a deal to sell her business, Armstrong Plumbing, had fallen through months earlier. She was also “really opposed to AI,” she told Fortune. She feared it would take her people and “take all the jobs.”

The visitors were AJ Jain and Aditya Ketkar, two engineers in their mid-twenties whose energy startup had just fizzled. They had spent that spring walking into about 140 contractors’ shops across Northern California, carrying a diary instead of laptops and offering no sales pitch.

“People were not treating us like salesmen,” Jain said. “Curious kids was, like, our persona,”

They had built exactly one thing worth showing: an automated appointment-reminder call for a San Francisco electrician.

Two years later, their company, Broccoli AI, has raised $52 million across its Series A and Series B. Khosla Ventures led both rounds, with Y Combinator and Operator Partners also participating. The raise was $22 million in Series A and $30 million in Series B, nine months apart, Jain, the company’s cofounder and CEO, told Fortune.

The Series A had not previously been announced. Broccoli is valued at $300 million post-money, according to a person familiar with the matter (Broccoli declined to comment on its valuation). The company had earlier raised $1.5 million in a seed round after going through Y Combinator.

And Marcelle Flowers is now working with the company. She got an apartment in San Francisco to work for them, and her life changed.

“If you had told me that I’d be running an AI company in the heart of San Francisco I would have laughed you out of the room,” Flowers said. “Like, furthest thing from my mind.”

Broccoli sells AI agents to plumbing, HVAC, and electrical companies. They answer inbound calls, book jobs directly into the scheduling software the contractor already uses, follow up on open estimates, and renew service memberships.

The company says more than 1,500 businesses now use it, including Ace Hardware Home Services, Mr. Electric, and Any Hour Group. In the past seven months it has added roofing, pool care, garage doors, home improvement, and exteriors.

Revenue has tripled since the Series A, Jain said, and headcount has grown from 15 people as of 12 months ago to more than 150. The company said the new money will go toward hiring engineers and salespeople as well as speeding up product development.

Owners wanted someone to answer the phone after the office emptied out at 5 p.m., close the books, and chase the estimates technicians wrote up, Jain said. The company says its AI does work equivalent to roughly 30% of a typical contractor’s office staff.

Jain, 27, is the first engineer in a family of business owners on both sides. He and Ketkar met at BITS Pilani in India in 2016 and have been starting companies together since 2017: a delivery app for closed college campuses, an interview-prep boot camp, and, after Y Combinator, a universal API for electric vehicles that took them to London. They signed eight customers there in two years. “We couldn’t scale that business, even after raising a seed round from YC,” Jain said.

They arrived in San Francisco in January 2024. That May and June they went door to door across the Bay Area, then Stockton, Lodi, Modesto, and Sacramento. They wanted an owner to build with.

At the utilities they had worked with before, Jain explained, he used to deal with product managers at 5,000-person companies. A contractor-owner, on the other hand, “cares about solving their customer’s problem.” Owners took them along on smoke breaks and told them how their fathers had started the business.

“The surprising thing is the American Dream is still alive,” Jain said, describing himself and Ketkar as two curious strangers who were met with trust and openness. “No one looked at our accents, our color.”

The turning point was when they met Flowers, who gave them five minutes that changed their lives, Jain said. It was eerie since it almost didn’t happen; Armstrong Plumbing was the only cold call they made twice.

They played her a recording of their one product, an automated call reminding customers of upcoming appointments. Flowers had just lost the employee who made those calls for her shop and hadn’t replaced her. “That hooks me,” she said.

Once the product worked for Flowers, her word of mouth took Broccoli from one customer to 10, and the door-knocking stopped. “She was the operator who helped us create this,” Jain said. “She’s the soul of the company.”

To understand this unlikely alliance, it helps to understand where Flowers came from. Born in 1963, she grew up in a blue-collar family in Anaheim, Calif., one of five children. Her father was a commercial plumber who built restaurants, hotels, and schools, and plumbers were regulars at the family breakfast table, while her mother stayed home. “Very, very much Brady Bunch family,” Flowers said.

She was the middle child and the “hell-raiser.” At 14, she sat her parents down at dinner and told them they were done raising her. “From here on out, I got this,” she recalled saying, describing herself as “barely a high school graduate.” She got pregnant at 19, had her son at 20, and raised him as a single mother. “I really went sideways for a while,” she said. She found her faith at 26.

She has a name for that stretch of life, roughly ages 16 to 26: “the stupid stage.” Decades of hiring young tradesmen gave her patience for men still in it. “I have a lot of grace for people because I was one of those,” she said.

She joined her father’s company in 1995, then opened its residential service-and-repair business in 2011. She said she grew it from about $1 million to $8 million in seven years with no outside c...

news.article_content_zh:
当马赛尔·弗劳尔斯的工作人员告诉她，有两名学生正在她位于萨克拉门托的管道店的柜台前等候时，她抓起了钱包。她以为他们正在为一支足球队出售巧克力棒。

“我真的说，你有五分钟的时间，”现年62岁的弗劳尔斯回忆说。那是2024年6月，几个月前，她出售公司阿姆斯特朗管道（Armstrong Plumbing）的交易告吹。她告诉《财富》杂志（Fortune），她也“非常反对人工智能”。她担心它会夺走她的员工，“夺走所有的工作”。

来访者是 AJ Jain 和 Aditya Ketkar，这两位二十五岁左右的工程师，他们的能源初创公司刚刚失败。那年春天，他们走进了北加州大约 140 家承包商的商店，携带的是日记本而不是笔记本电脑，也没有进行任何推销。

“人们不把我们当推销员，”杰恩说。“好奇的孩子是我们的角色，”

他们只做了一件值得展示的东西：一个旧金山电工的自动预约提醒电话。

Two years later, their company, Broccoli AI, has raised $52 million across its Series A and Series B. Khosla Ventures led both rounds, with Y Combinator and Operator Partners also participating. The raise was $22 million in Series A and $30 million in Series B, nine months apart, Jain, the company’s cofounder and CEO, told Fortune.

A轮融资此前并未公布。据一位知情人士透露，收购完成后，西兰花的估值为3亿美元（西兰花拒绝就其估值置评）。该公司早些时候在Y Combinator的种子轮融资中获得了150万美元。

马塞勒·弗劳尔斯（Marcelle Flowers）现在在该公司工作。她在旧金山找到了一套公寓，为他们工作，她的生活发生了变化。

“如果你告诉我，我将在旧金山市中心经营一家人工智能公司，我一定会把你从房间里笑出来，”弗劳尔斯说。 “就像，离我脑海最远的事情。”

西兰花向管道、暖通空调和电气公司出售人工智能代理。他们接听来电，直接在承包商已经使用的调度软件中预定工作，跟进公开评估，并更新服务会员资格。

The company says more than 1,500 businesses now use it, including Ace Hardware Home Services, Mr. Electric, and Any Hour Group. In the past seven months it has added roofing, pool care, garage doors, home improvement, and exteriors.

Jain说，自A轮融资以来，公司收入增加了两倍，员工人数也从12个月前的15人增加到150多人。该公司表示，这笔新资金将用于招聘工程师和销售人员，以及加快产品开发。

news.title_en: Letter: the White House argues it doesn't have to share the full draft of its voluntary AI testing framework, citing national security and commercial exemptions (Leo Schwartz/The Information)
news.author: The Information
news.content_snippet: The Trump administration declined to produce key documents related to its voluntary AI testing framework …
news.summary_en: In an official response, the White House declined to disclose the complete draft and key records of its voluntary AI testing framework, citing exemptions for national security and confidential commercial information. The administration maintained that withholding the documentation is justified under federal disclosure protections. The move reflects an ongoing effort to introduce voluntary safety standards while shielding tech giants' proprietary algorithms and sensitive defense equities.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 白宫在针对相关记录披露要求的官方回函中，正式拒绝提供其自愿性人工智能测试框架的完整草案及核心文件。官方给出的法律依据是，这批关键记录受到联邦信息披露法中关于国家安全和企业商业机密豁免条款的保护。此举反映出联邦政府在推行AI行业自愿性审查的同时，极力避免强制科技巨头公开底层技术机密或触碰国防敏感信息。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: In an official response, the White House declined to disclose the complete draft and key records of its voluntary AI testing framework, citing exemptions for national security and confidential commercial information. The administration maintained that withholding the documentation is justified under federal disclosure protections. The move reflects an ongoing effort to introduce voluntary safety standards while shielding tech giants' proprietary algorithms and sensitive defense equities.

ai_analysis.insight_en: Coupling 'voluntary testing' with 'national security exemptions' is classic regulatory theater for letting Big Tech grade its own homework in the dark. It postures as tough on frontier AI safety while ensuring Silicon Valley's corporate secrets remain untouchable behind the ultimate all-purpose shield.

news.title: Hyperbolic, which lets companies rent AI compute across ~30 neoclouds, raised a $30M Series A-1 led by Lip-Bu Tan's Walden Catalyst; it has raised $50M to date (Geoff Weiss/Business Insider)
news.title_en: Hyperbolic, which lets companies rent AI compute across ~30 neoclouds, raised a $30M Series A-1 led by Lip-Bu Tan's Walden Catalyst; it has raised $50M to date (Geoff Weiss/Business Insider)
news.author: Business Insider
news.article_content:
Save Saved As companies scramble for computing power, one challenge is that AI cloud providers, or neoclouds, use a mix of different chips, networking, and software. Hyperbolic helps customers find compute resources from different providers and creates software that makes it easier to use them all, rather than dealing with each one separately.

"It's been a really fragmented market that makes the customer experience really painful," said 31-year-old founder and CEO Jasper Zhang.

Hyperbolic also wants to let customers resell compute that they're paying for but no longer need.

The four-year-old startup works closely with about 30 neoclouds, including WhiteFiber and Vector Core Compute. It says it has roughly $200 million worth of compute connected to its software annually.

Hyperbolic previously raised a $12 million Series A round in 2024, led by Variant and Polychain Capital, following a $7 million seed round earlier that year. The company expects to have 50 employees by the end of the year and will use its funding to expand software tools for managing AI chips across different neoclouds.

Zhang said the company is aiming for $150 million in annual recurring revenue by the end of the year and is already breaking even. More than 250,000 developers, including teams at Modal, Higgsfield, and Daytona, use Hyperbolic.

Before founding the company, Zhang worked as a quantitative researcher at Citadel Securities. As Wall Street explores ways to financialize AI chips, he said his startup's plans to let companies resell unused compute could help pave the way for a futures market.

Here's a look at the pitch deck Hyperbolic used to raise its $30 million Series A-1. Slides have been redacted so that the deck can be shared publicly.

news.article_content_zh:
随着公司争夺计算能力，人工智能云提供商（或 Neocloud）混合使用不同的芯片、网络和软件，这是一个挑战。双曲线帮助客户找到来自不同提供商的计算资源，并创建软件以更轻松地使用所有资源，而不是单独处理每一项资源。

31 岁的创始人兼首席执行官 Jasper Zhang 表示：“这是一个非常分散的市场，让客户体验非常痛苦。”

Hyperbolic 还希望让客户转售他们已付费但不再需要的计算设备。

这家成立四年的初创公司与大约 30 个 neocloud 密切合作，其中包括 WhiteFiber 和 Vector Core Compute。该公司表示，每年与其软件连接的计算价值约为 2 亿美元。

Hyperbolic 此前在 2024 年筹集了 1200 万美元的 A 轮融资，由 Variant 和 Polychain Capital 领投，此前该轮融资为 700 万美元。该公司预计到今年年底将拥有 50 名员工，并将利用其资金扩展用于跨不同 Neocloud 管理 AI 芯片的软件工具。

张说，公司的目标是到年底实现年度经常性收入 1.5 亿美元，并且已经实现收支平衡。超过 250,000 名开发人员（包括 Modal、Higgsfield 和 Daytona 的团队）使用 Hyperbolic。

在创立公司之前，张先生曾在 Citadel 证券担任量化研究员。在华尔街探索人工智能芯片金融化的方法之际，他表示，他的初创公司计划让公司转售未使用的计算设备，这可能有助于为期货市场铺平道路。

news.title: A look at Binance's efforts to contain the hack, including creating a global war room of ~100 people, coordinating with other crypto firms and the FBI, and more (Bloomberg)
news.title_en: A look at Binance's efforts to contain the hack, including creating a global war room of ~100 people, coordinating with other crypto firms and the FBI, and more (Bloomberg)
news.author: Bloomberg
news.article_content:
The biggest crypto hack in history began with a rehearsal.

As trading hummed along on Binance at midweek, hackers were quietly running sequences of code on accounts they controlled on the Ethereum blockchain — just a couple dollars or so at a time. According to cybersecurity analysts, they were testing a program designed to seize control of accounts owned by the world’s largest crypto exchange and smuggle their contents elsewhere.

news.title: How IShowSpeed became YouTube's top livestreamer with 62M+ subscribers, as his 24/7 "IRL streams" that last days mingle childlike wonder with teenage mischief (Jon Caramanica/New York Times)
news.title_en: How IShowSpeed became YouTube's top livestreamer with 62M+ subscribers, as his 24/7 "IRL streams" that last days mingle childlike wonder with teenage mischief (Jon Caramanica/New York Times)
news.author: New York Times
news.article_content:
Livestreaming is unstoppably ascendant — and often boring. IShowSpeed became the king of the form by bringing his act into the real world.

IShowSpeed in Las Vegas during the Speed Does America bus tour.Credit...Malike Sidibe for The New York Times

Jon Caramanica traveled with Speed to seven states over the past 18 months, including four days and three nights on the Speed Does America tour.

With seven minutes left in the second quarter of their fall 2025 homecoming game, the Custer High Wildcats of Custer, S.D. — population 2,341 — were down 36-0 to the St. Thomas More Cavaliers. If they gave up another 14 points, the game would be over by league mercy rules.

In the back of an S.U.V. speeding down Route 16A, Ames Ward, a senior producer for the livestream superstar IShowSpeed, was counting the minutes, too. He was exchanging direct messages with the Custer High media class’s Instagram account, trying to gauge whether Speed’s caravan might make it to the game before it ended.

Streaming has become one of the dominant modes of entertainment on the internet, with hundreds of thousands of people worldwide broadcasting their lives in real time via platforms like Twitch, Kick and YouTube. These performances are largely lo-fi affairs, a monitor-mounted camera trained on a person gaming or watching soccer or playing poker. A set of open portals into long-form thumb twiddling. Even many of the biggest livestream personalities — the antic hangout host Kai Cenat, the professional gamer Ninja, the artist and producer PlaqueBoyMax — broadcast primarily from their desks.

Speed has taken one of the most limp modes of entertainment and put it in Technicolor, bringing his cameras and his curiosity out into the world on a series of dynamically disorderly quests all over the globe. In the last two years, he has visited over 100 countries across five continents — Chile, Zambia, New Zealand, Ethiopia, Turkey, Uruguay and more. Trailed by a rotation of camerapeople and flanked by security guards, he moves around the world and invents his entertainment from the raw cloth of human interaction.

His streams function on multiple levels: travelogue, durational art piece, technological stunt, family sitcom, brandable marketing opportunity. Each stream — some last a few hours, some last days — is a one-man play, with improvisational work contributed by umpteen secondary characters who flock from their homes to see him, sometimes by the thousands, or watch from home, sometimes up to a million at a time. In Speed’s hands, livestreaming multiplies the spontaneity of social media by the intimacy of podcasting: The viewer is thereby transformed from consumer to sidekick, a remora hitching along for an unpredictable ride.

news.title: Saudi Aramco acquires a 49% stake in AI startup Humain, contributing ~$2.6B in cash in 2026 plus AI, compute, and digital assets; Saudi Arabia's PIF retains 51% (Dean Takahashi/GamesBeat)
news.title_en: Saudi Aramco acquires a 49% stake in AI startup Humain, contributing ~$2.6B in cash in 2026 plus AI, compute, and digital assets; Saudi Arabia's PIF retains 51% (Dean Takahashi/GamesBeat)
news.author: GamesBeat
news.article_content:
Saudi Arabia-based oil and energy firm Aramco has acquired a 49% stake in AI firm Humain for $2.6 billion today.

The Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund owns 51% of the Humain, while Aramco now owns 49%$, through a wholly owned subsidiary.

The transaction will further accelerate Humain’s growth and advance its full range of AI capabilities globally, with PIF and Aramco contributing AI assets, capabilities, and talent.

The transaction will accelerate Humain’s ambition to build a globally competitive, integrated AI ecosystem spanning the full stack: from data centers and high-performance compute to advanced models, applications, and industry solutions. Additionally, it will further enable Humain’s plans to develop data center capacity by 2030 and deliver solutions that help the public and private sectors to deploy AI at scale.

The transaction builds on Saudi Arabia’s efforts to further enable the development and deployment of the most advanced data and AI technologies while attracting talent and investment opportunities.

PIF’s strategy for AI and the digital economy benefits from Saudi Arabia’s position as a globally competitive market through innovation and capacity building. Partnering with Aramco in Humain aligns with PIF’s 2026-2030 strategy, which aims to deepen integration across economic ecosystems, expand opportunities with the private sector, and accelerate the growth of national companies into globally competitive leaders.

Aramco is expected to leverage Humain’s AI infrastructure to translate advanced AI capabilities into industrial applications, further enhancing its global ecosystem and operations. Aramco, together with its affiliates, will benefit as a shareholder and strategic partner from HUMAIN’s advanced AI infrastructure and services. With opportunities for revenue growth andattractive margins, this partnership is expected to enhance Aramco’s monetization of existing AI and digital assets, support its broader strategy, and complement its core energy business.

Yazeed A. Al-Humied, Deputy Governor and Head of MENA Investments at PIF, said in a statement: “Bringing PIF and Aramco’s AI portfolio of investments together under Humain creates a powerful synergy that fuels talent growth, technological advancement, and intellectual property creation.”

Al-Humied added, “Fully aligned with PIF’s strategic objectives, this transaction accelerates Humain’s growth into a global leader in the sector, strengthening AI as an enabler of PIF’s six ecosystems and further expanding private sector participation across our portfolio while advancing the development of cutting edge technologies in Saudi Arabia.”

Amin H. Nasser, Aramco president and CEO, said in a statement, “The Humain deal is very important to Aramco, building on the company’s long track record of innovation and technology. We are proud of our achieved progress in developing and deploying advanced digital and AI technologies to enhance performance across the oil and gas sectors.”

Nasser said that since 2023, Aramco has achieved $11.3 billion in Technology Realized Value, with a significant portion coming from AI solutions.

Nasser added, “This partnership with PIF strengthens Aramco’s position as a global technology leader and AI powerhouse, while laying the foundation for localizing the AI industry and enabling faster, more integrated, and scalable deployment of AI systems. AI will therefore play a vital role in the future of business. We are delighted to collaborate with PIF to help shape the future of AI regionally and globally.”

The transaction involves approximately SAR 9.9 billion ($2.6 billion) in cash contributions in 2026 from Aramco to Humain, in addition to AI, compute, and digital assets.

Launched in May 2025, Humain is building full-stack AI capabilities across four core areas: next generation data centers; hyper-performance infrastructure and cloud platforms; advanced AI models including ALLAM, one of the world’s most powerful multimodal Arabic large language models (LLMs); and transformative AI solutions.

Through the deployment of 3 gigawatts of AI data center capacity by 2030, Humain is rapidly scaling to meet growing regional and global demand for AI compute, with the aim of becoming one of the leading exporters of AI globally.

Saudi Arabia-based Aramco is one of the world’s leading integrated energy and chemicals companies, creating value across the hydrocarbon chain and delivering societal and economic benefits to people and communities around the globe. And the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund (PIF) is one of the world’s largest investors, with a long-term investment strategy to further drive the economic transformation of Saudi Arabia and deliver sustainable financial returns.

news.article_content_zh:
总部位于沙特阿拉伯的石油和能源公司阿美公司今天以 26 亿美元收购了人工智能公司 Humain 49% 的股份。

沙特阿拉伯公共投资基金拥有 Humain 51% 的股份，而沙特阿美公司目前通过全资子公司拥有 49% 的股份。

此次交易将进一步加速 Humain 的增长，并在全球范围内提升其全方位的人工智能能力，PIF 和阿美公司将贡献人工智能资产、能力和人才。

此次交易将加速Humain建立具有全球竞争力的、涵盖全栈的集成人工智能生态系统的雄心：从数据中心和高性能计算到先进模型、应用程序和行业解决方案。此外，它将进一步实现 Humain 到 2030 年开发数据中心容量的计划，并提供帮助公共和私营部门大规模部署人工智能的解决方案。

此次交易建立在沙特阿拉伯努力进一步促进最先进数据和人工智能技术的开发和部署，同时吸引人才和投资机会的基础上。

PIF 的人工智能和数字经济战略受益于沙特阿拉伯通过创新和能力建设作为全球竞争市场的地位。与沙特阿美在 Humain 的合作符合 PIF 的 2026-2030 战略，该战略旨在深化经济生态系统的一体化，扩大与私营部门的机会，并加速国有企业成长为具有全球竞争力的领导者。

沙特阿美预计将利用Humain的人工智能基础设施，将先进的人工智能能力转化为工业应用，进一步增强其全球生态系统和运营。阿美公司及其附属公司将作为股东和战略合作伙伴从 HUMAIN 先进的人工智能基础设施和服务中受益。凭借收入增长的机会和有吸引力的利润率，这一合作伙伴关系预计将增强阿美公司现有人工智能和数字资产的货币化，支持其更广泛的战略，并补充其核心能源业务。

PIF 副行长兼中东和北非投资主管 Yazeed A. Al-Humied 在一份声明中表示：“将 PIF 和阿美石油公司的人工智能投资组合纳入 Humain 旗下，可产生强大的协同效应，推动人才增长、技术进步和知识产权创造。”

Al-Humied 补充道：“此次交易完全符合 PIF 的战略目标，加速 Humain 成长为该行业的全球领导者，加强人工智能作为 PIF 六个生态系统推动者的地位，并进一步扩大私营部门在我们投资组合中的参与，同时推动沙特阿拉伯尖端技术的发展。”

沙特阿美总裁兼首席执行官阿明·H·纳赛尔 (Amin H. Nasser) 在一份声明中表示：“Humain 交易对沙特阿美来说非常重要，它建立在公司长期创新和技术记录的基础上。我们为我们在开发和部署先进数字和人工智能技术以提高石油和天然气行业绩效方面取得的进展感到自豪。”

纳赛尔表示，自 2023 年以来，阿美公司已实现 113 亿美元的技术实现价值，其中很大一部分来自人工智能解决方案。

Nasser 补充道：“与 PIF 的合作巩固了阿美公司作为全球技术领导者和人工智能强国的地位，同时为人工智能行业本地化以及实现更快、更集成和可扩展的人工智能系统部署奠定了基础。因此，人工智能将在未来的商业中发挥至关重要的作用。我们很高兴与 PIF 合作，帮助塑造区域和全球人工智能的未来。”

除了人工智能、计算和数字资产之外，该交易还涉及阿美公司在 2026 年向 Humain 提供约 99 亿沙特里亚尔（26 亿美元）的现金捐助。

Humain 于 2025 年 5 月推出，正在构建跨四个核心领域的全栈人工智能功能：下一代数据中心；超高性能基础设施和云平台；先进的人工智能模型，包括 ALLAM，世界上最强大的多模式阿拉伯语大语言模型 (LLM) 之一；和变革性的人工智能解决方案。

通过到 2030 年部署 3 吉瓦的人工智能数据中心容量，Humain 正在快速扩展，以满足区域和全球对人工智能计算不断增长的需求，目标是成为全球领先的人工智能出口商之一。

总部位于沙特阿拉伯的阿美公司是世界领先的综合能源和化学品公司之一，在整个碳氢化合物链上创造价值，并为全球人民和社区带来社会和经济效益。沙特阿拉伯公共投资基金（PIF）是全球最大的投资者之一，其长期投资战略旨在进一步推动沙特阿拉伯的经济转型并带来可持续的财务回报。

news.title: How "get-paid-to" apps like Freecash, briefly a top five App Store app in September, pay users small sums to play games and help publishers find big spenders (John Herrman/New York Magazine)
news.title_en: How "get-paid-to" apps like Freecash, briefly a top five App Store app in September, pay users small sums to play games and help publishers find big spenders (John Herrman/New York Magazine)
news.author: New York Magazine
news.article_content:
Find this story in your account’s ‘Saved for Later’ section.

Jeremiah tried out a few of these apps. They had names like KashKick, Swagbucks, and Mistplay. After wasting hours on games in KashKick for low payouts with too many restrictions and caveats, he switched to an app called Freecash. Most of the featured games are traps, he said — the rewards decrease as you play and give you unreachable targets — but he eventually put together a routine. At 44, he had spent years playing World of Warcraft and ’90s strategy games before it. “I can grind,” he said, “and that’s what most of these games are.” Now, he was grinding for cash by playing iPhone-era strategy games like Rise of Kingdoms, which involves building cities and battling other players for virtual resources and land. By assembling his army and succeeding in the game, he could eventually reach goals in Freecash, then redeem them for a few real dollars. Beyond his gaming background, Jeremiah had the time — he worked in farming for years in eastern North Carolina but had since gone on disability — so he professionalized his operation. He played multiple games at once: Age of Dragons, Legend of Mushroom, and countless similar ones that would pop up in Freecash’s list of offers with better terms. He set up multiple profiles on a folding Samsung phone where he could check on his progress and track his earning tasks at the same time.

Jeremiah’s fate within the games, which were themselves about the slow and precarious accumulation of virtual resources, soon had real stakes. He started setting timers so he wouldn’t miss chances to upgrade or progress. He also had to be constantly vigilant against raids, in which other players, some grinding for credit in apps like Freecash themselves, could attack and steal in-game resources, indirectly robbing Jeremiah of real earnings in the process. He defends himself by working with a clan of allied players gathered from the strange and ephemeral social environments that briefly materialize at different levels of the get-paid-to, or GPT, app ecosystem. “90 percent of the time, you get up on a server that’s full of Brazilians, but there are also a lot of people from Malaysia and the Philippines,” he said. With the arrival of automatic AI translation, these in-game chats have become somewhat more useful and less alienating. “We’ll discuss the strategy for getting higher on the game,” he added. Some are in it for the money. Others are just addicted.

For mobile-game companies, apps like Freecash are a way to buy downloads but also to filter their customers, paying out small amounts to find out which might end up spending even more. (The industry borrows a term, whales, from casinos for the big spenders who make the business model work.) Earning money by playing these games is hard. Spending it is easy. Using real money to buy in-game resources in Rise of Kingdom, for example, can speed up progress and increase your power in the game, allowing you to skip over hours of play or to dominate other players. If you’re using Freecash, this may get you closer to a real payout. But progress is often elusive and hard to track. It’s easy to overspend in pursuit of slippery goals or to become straightforwardly addicted, disengaging from the get-paid-to ecosystem entirely.

If players do eventually make enough money to withdraw, they’ll often be greeted with a string of solicitations to funnel their funds through an affiliated gambling platform like Stake, where they’ll be enticed by new and arcane promotions, rules, and fine print. Even for a grinder, it’s a grind. Since Jeremiah started keeping track and paying for some of his in-app purchases with other GPT apps like Scrambly, he has cleared $8,000 in total payouts. Still, after weeks or months of attention-draining, repetitive check-ins and resets and blurred-together earnings, wins, and losses, the notion that you’re getting paid to do things you would be doing anyway, or getting “paid to scroll,” sounds absurd. This is a common complaint in get-paid-to advice communities, which suggest that far more people wash out of these apps than stick with them. “They make gaming a grind and not fun anymore,” wrote another user on Reddit. “They are greedy af and have unrealistic timelines and crap payouts.” Jeremiah still plays mainstream games in his spare time. As for the hypermonetized slopware games that send him notifications all day and night: “It’s work.”

For Jeremiah, the get-paid-to regimen is working well enough that he hasn’t called it quits yet, even if it wears him out sometimes. “I’m on my phone all day anyway,” he said, “and it’s not the only thing I’m doing.” A few days before I spoke to him, he won a bet at cash-out and made a few hundred dollars. He was relieved, he said, and planned to take a few days off.

Apps such as Freecash have been around for more than a decade, but they’ve recently become harder to miss, appearing frequently in the App Store charts — Freecash briefly broke into the top five in September — and meeting the American public at a moment of intense economic worry and disillusionment. Hiring is low, and the entire economy is being propped up by a multitrillion-dollar bet on a general-purpose job-automating machine. Even more people than usual are worried about work, specifically and in general. The global financial crisis was followed by the rise of the gig economy. As Americans clench through the late Trump years — and inflation and high interest rates and the AI boom — it’s reasonable to wonder if a newer, harsher, and more convoluted vision of gig work is what’s waiting for us on the other side.

Mostly, though, it’s because of the advertising, which is all over social media. According to Appfigures, Freecash grew from fewer than a million downloads in October 2025 to 6 million in February 2026, boosted by a flood of ads that promised, for example, up to $35 an hour to watch TikTok, while giving users the impression that they would...

news.article_content_zh:
在您帐户的“保存以供稍后使用”部分中找到这个故事。

耶利米尝试了其中一些应用程序。他们的名字包括 KashKick、Swagbucks 和 Mistplay。在 KashKick 游戏中浪费了数小时的时间，因为支付率低、限制和警告太多，他转向了一款名为 Freecash 的应用程序。他说，大多数特色游戏都是陷阱——随着你玩游戏，奖励会减少，并给你无法达到的目标——但他最终整理出了一个例程。 44 岁的他已经玩了多年《魔兽世界》和之前的 90 年代策略游戏。 “我可以磨练，”他说，“这就是大多数游戏的本质。”现在，他通过玩《万国崛起》等 iPhone 时代的策略游戏来赚钱，游戏涉及建造城市并与其他玩家争夺虚拟资源和土地。通过组建他的军队并在游戏中取得成功，他最终可以实现自由现金的目标，然后将其兑换成一些真实的美元。除了游戏背景之外，耶利米还有时间——他在北卡罗来纳州东部务农多年，但后来残疾了——所以他将自己的经营专业化。他同时玩了多款游戏：《龙腾世纪》、《蘑菇传奇》，以及无数类似的游戏，这些游戏会以更好的条件出现在 Freecash 的优惠列表中。他在折叠式三星手机上设置了多个配置文件，可以在其中检查自己的进度并同时跟踪他的收入任务。

耶利米在游戏中的命运，本身就是关于虚拟资源的缓慢而不稳定的积累，很快就产生了真正的利害关系。他开始设置计时器，这样他就不会错过升级或进步的机会。他还必须时刻警惕突袭，其他玩家（其中一些在 Freecash 等应用程序中磨练信用）可能会攻击并窃取游戏内资源，从而间接剥夺 Jeremiah 在此过程中的实际收入。他通过与一群来自奇怪而短暂的社交环境的盟友合作来保护自己，这些环境短暂地出现在付费应用程序生态系统的不同层面。 “90% 的情况下，你所在的服务器都是巴西人，但也有很多来自马来西亚和菲律宾的人，”他说。随着自动人工智能翻译的到来，这些游戏内聊天变得更加有用，也不再那么疏远。 “我们将讨论在比赛中取得更高成绩的策略，”他补充道。有些人是为了钱。其他人只是上瘾了。

对于手机游戏公司来说，像 Freecash 这样的应用程序是一种购买下载的方式，同时也是过滤客户的一种方式，通过支付少量费用来找出哪些人最终可能会花费更多。 （该行业从赌场借用了一个术语“鲸鱼”，指的是使商业模式发挥作用的大手笔消费者。）通过玩这些游戏来赚钱很困难。花钱很容易。例如，在《王国崛起》中使用真实货币购买游戏内资源可以加快进度并增强您在游戏中的力量，让您可以跳过几个小时的游戏时间或统治其他玩家。如果您使用 Freecash，这可能会让您更接近真正的支付。但进展往往难以捉摸且难以追踪。为了追求难以捉摸的目标，人们很容易超支，或者直接上瘾，完全脱离付费生态系统。

如果玩家最终赚到足够的钱来提款，他们通常会收到一连串的邀请，要求他们通过 Stake 等附属赌博平台转移资金，在那里他们会被新的、神秘的促销、规则和细则所吸引。即使对于研磨机来说，这也是一种研磨。自从 Jeremiah 开始使用 Scrambly 等其他 GPT 应用程序跟踪并支付一些应用内购买费用以来，他已支付了 8,000 美元的总支出。尽管如此，经过数周或数月的注意力耗尽、重复的签到和重置以及模糊的收益、胜利和损失之后，你会因为做你无论如何都会做的事情而获得报酬，或者“获得报酬来滚动”的想法听起来很荒谬。这是付费咨询社区中常见的抱怨，这表明放弃这些应用程序的人比坚持使用它们的人要多得多。 Reddit 上的另一位用户写道：“他们让游戏变成一种苦差事，不再有趣。” “他们很贪婪，有着不切实际的时间表和垃圾支出。” Jeremiah 在业余时间仍然玩主流游戏。至于那些日夜不停地向他发送通知的超赚钱的垃圾软件游戏：“这是工作。”

对于耶利米来说，这种付费养生法效果很好，他还没有放弃，尽管有时会让他精疲力竭。 “无论如何，我一整天都在玩手机，”他说，“而且这不是我唯一做的事情。”在我和他谈话的前几天，他在兑现赌注中赢了，赚了几百美元。他说，他松了一口气，并打算休息几天。

Freecash 等应用程序已经存在了十多年，但最近它们变得越来越难以错过，频繁出现在 App Store 排行榜中——Freecash 在 9 月份曾一度跻身前五——并在美国公众对经济产生强烈担忧和幻灭的时刻出现。招聘人数很少，整个经济是靠对通用工作自动化机器的数万亿美元赌注支撑的。比平常更多的人担心工作，无论是具体的还是总体的。全球金融危机之后，零工经济兴起。随着美国人紧握特朗普的晚年——通货膨胀、高利率和人工智能的繁荣——我们有理由怀疑，在另一边等待我们的是否是一种更新、更严厉、更复杂的零工工作愿景。

不过，这主要是因为社交媒体上到处都是广告。根据 Appfigures 的数据，Freecash 的下载量从 2025 年 10 月的不到 100 万次增长到 2026 年 2 月的 600 万次，这得益于大量广告的推动，这些广告承诺每小时观看 TikTok 的费用高达 35 美元，同时给用户一种他们会以某种方式为这家社交媒体公司工作的印象。据《连线》报道，TikTok 因具有误导性而撤下了其中一些广告；最终，苹果和谷歌都暂时从他们的商店中启动了该应用程序。现在，应用程序又回来了，广告也回来了。

居住在俄亥俄州的 IT 和营销专业人士斯科特·斯威尼 (Scott Sweeney) 多年来一直了解这个奇怪的行业，但没有理由参与其中。然后，在从事科技工作 11 年后，他被解雇了。 “在我看来，我正在努力缩小一个小差距，”他说。他有遣散费，但还有一个孩子。所以他尝试了这些应用程序。 “最早的经历非常令人沮丧，”他说。他补充说，Freecash 等应用程序是“门户”。 “你投入了最初的努力，这表明你只花了 15 分钟，就赚了 3 美元。”他说，大多数应用程序都是“提前加载的”——机会很快就会枯竭，很快你就会花费“大量的时间和工作来赚钱”。

我自己在 Freecash 上的短暂经历立即证实了这一点。它建议我下载的第一个应用程序是迪士尼纸牌，这是一款来自美国最健康的企业集团之一的看似简单的游戏。

起初，游戏运行起来没有任何摩擦，处理简单的画面并提供频繁的提示、奖励卡，所有这些都似乎对我有利。在后台，我正在积累数千枚米老鼠硬币，这是我几分钟前就知道的货币。事情很快就变慢了，游戏的场景拉长了，奖金变得不那么频繁，我的抽奖感觉也更糟了。回到 Freecash，我的第一笔 12 美元在一小时内就到了。但很明显，要达到 25 美元的提款门槛，还需要数千次点击和数百次小额签到。当然，如果我想跳过，我可以支付：花 5 美元，我可能会到达迪士尼纸牌的下一个里程碑，这可以让我用 Freecash 兑现。 （迪士尼向我提供的第一个应用内购买优惠是 200,000 虚拟币的“超值”套餐，售价 49.99 美元。）或者我可以像 Reddit 上的玩家一样苦苦挣扎，一个月“几乎没有出门”，花了大约 60 美元，然后无法兑现他们的 600 美元收入。 “同时在一个随机的加油站工作可能会赚更多的钱，”他们写道。 “至少我实际上会得到报酬，哈哈。”

斯威尼没有时间做这些。他决定首先专注于调查，这是许多付费应用程序中的另一个可用选项。通过回答市场研究问题或回应民意调查，他可以在忙碌的一天中的闲暇时间赚几美元。 （他说，其中相当多的任务只是“询问美国政治中的恒温意见”，从一群至少在手机上被不良氛围包围的人那里进行广泛的氛围检查。）他还收到了很多微任务，其背后的机制非常清晰。他可能会被要求下载一个应用程序并花五分钟使用它，这将为开发人员带来有利的参与度衡量。有流行的数据收集应用程序，例如 Fetch 和 Receipt Hog，它们为共享收据提供付款，购买特定产品的费率更高。还有一些更新的、看似以人工智​​能为中心的付费应用机会。 “你会得到一个类似‘拍一堆自拍照，并以 5 美元的价格放弃你的个人生物识别信息’之类的任务，”斯威尼说。

他也开始将这项活动更像是一份工作，进一步从业余任务、分层积分和奖励转向更明确形式的微型零工工作。 iVueit 等应用程序为商业客户提供“按需财产检查”，例如“验证当前状况”或“远程监控零售执行情况”，它会为他分配附近的任务，他可以在游泳课期间走出去拍摄，例如，Dollar General 外面的景观状况； Prolific 等公司为“人工智能判断”提供报酬，最终将其输入到谷歌和 OpenAI 等公司的模型中。

“很多人正在转向这类工作，”斯威尼说。他表示，他们并没有忘记这样的工作有点自我消除的感觉，“而且知道你的注意力是他们唯一感兴趣的商品，这感觉不太好。”这些应用程序也不会让你忘记这一点：做这种零工工作就会面临无休无止的广告、令人困惑的促销和抽奖，以及一系列的条形图、旋转的轮子和五彩纸屑爆炸，营造出一种在实现遥不可及的目标的过程中不断移动和进步的感觉。 （对于任何使用过赌博应用程序或刚刚浏览过 Shein 或 Temu 的人来说，这可能听起来很熟悉。）

最后，斯威尼说，这并不特别重要。 “很多这样做的人只是想找到达到目的的方法，”他说，像他一样弥合差距，在家养育孩子，或者寻找一种不太具有破坏性的副业。当然，提供这些任务的公司对他们的各种“最终游戏”都讳莫如深，并且似乎对用户不尊重近乎蔑视。但他们正在付钱。

此后，斯威尼重新加入了传统劳动力队伍，但仍然在业余时间做一些任务性工作，留出收入来偿还债务或为家庭度假储蓄。在发现该领域更好的机会之前，他将自己的研究成果转化为一系列 Reddit 建议帖子，这些帖子引起了广泛关注：他将这些帖子变成了付费应用程序的在线指南，其中一些应用程序向他支付新用户的附属佣金。

人工智能领导者喜欢大声地想知道，一旦他们的产品能够完成我们今天认为的大部分或大部分工作，人类还剩下什么工作。付费应用程序提供了对剩下的内容的客观愿景：通过广告收获并转化为应用程序指标的原始注意力；旨在缩小机器能力差距的非分布、低上下文任务；消费者偏好的财产和表达，可用于改善营销。

但所有这些 TikTok 广告背后的真相并不是关于时间和劳动力价值的新颖论点，而是更熟悉的零和游戏。经过一段时间的尝试和错误，Jeremiah 的现金流转为正值，GPT 应用程序已成为他日常生活的主要部分。他的母亲注意到了，并认为她也会尝试一下。她登录了 Freecash，还接触了 Disney Solitaire，很快就上瘾了。 “这是一个巨大的陷阱，”他说。 “在我意识到之前，她已经花掉了 200 到 300 美元，只得到了 100 美元。”现在，收款模式的双方都在同一所房子里进行，所以他介入并访问了她的自由现金账户。他注意到，他们玩了很多相同的游戏，但作为新玩家，她经常得到更好的优惠和价格。她需要退后一步，...

news.title: A look at VC-backed glossy magazine Colossus, whose glowing profiles of Zuckerberg and other tech titans win industry praise, while Kara Swisher says it is PR (Andrew Fedorov/The San Francisco Standard)
news.title_en: A look at VC-backed glossy magazine Colossus, whose glowing profiles of Zuckerberg and other tech titans win industry praise, while Kara Swisher says it is PR (Andrew Fedorov/The San Francisco Standard)
news.author: The San Francisco Standard
news.article_content:
A venture capitalist’s glossy quarterly wants to be The New Yorker for tech billionaires.

Many media veterans doubt the profiles accomplish their subjects’ public relations goals. “It’s all well and good for the tech industry media bubble to have its own in-flight magazine, but audiences aren’t stupid,” Nilay Patel, editor-in-chief of The Verge, said in an email. “Writing a massive profile of Mark Zuckerberg in which … his staggering unpopularity with everyday Americans is treated as an unfortunate byproduct of his ambition just isn’t going to convince anyone of anything.

“If Mark actually wanted to be understood as he says he does, he’d sit down for a truly adversarial journalistic interview and try to make his case,” Patel added. “But I don’t think he can take the risk.”

Colossus is the brainchild of Patrick O’Shaughnessy, a Connecticut-raised heir to an oil fortune, who went to work for his father James’ firm, O’Shaughnessy Asset Management, in 2007. Patrick took over the company in 2018 and sold it four years later to Franklin Templeton. In 2016, he launched a podcast called “Invest Like the Best,” borrowing the title of a book his father published in 1994.

His guests on the podcast have included Berkshire Hathaway Vice Chairman Charlie Munger and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. In 2020, building on the success of “Invest Like the Best,” which O’Shaughnessy has said gets north of 100,000 downloads per episode, he launched a podcast network called Colossus, which now has shows like “Business Breakdowns” and “Founders.” The same year, he spun up a venture capital firm, Positive Sum.

“It’s actually great that venture capitalists are now writing all of the founder hagiography, because it means that when, inevitably, one of these people goes to prison, the blowback will not affect mainstream journalists,” said Casey Newton, founder of Platformer and cohost of the new NPR podcast, “Machine Gods.” “It will just affect the venture class, and they can take it.”

But Colossus is the first in this wave of VC-sponsored media to make a serious effort to ape the writing and photography of glossy magazines. “This kind of wet kiss has always existed, but it was never done this artfully,” said Samtani. “To be super clear, it is not journalism. It is positioned, oftentimes, as journalism. They hire journalists, but it is not journalism. Think of it as high-grade, tier-one content marketing.”

The upside is less for the magazine itself, Samtani explained, than for O’Shaughnessy’s venture firm. “Their economics are not media company economics. This is at least partly a clout exercise and an access game, and it’s a very smart one,” he said. “Media is an incredible way to create connections and develop your own influence.”

Notably, O’Shaughnessy failed to absorb the first paragraph of Remnick’s introduction, which establishes the form’s ethos. He wrote that The New Yorker’s founding editor, Harold Ross, “prized intimacy and wit over biographical completeness or, God forbid, unabashed hero worship. Ross told his writers and editors that, above all, he wanted to get away from what he was reading in the other magazines — all the ‘Horatio Alger’ stuff.”

The typical Colossus profile follows the classic Alger trajectory: scrappy kid overcomes adversity to achieve success. But Colossus adds a twist befitting our nepo-baby era. Its subjects tend to be born not in rags but with relative riches. Their great accomplishment is to accumulate even more money than their well-off parents.

To fit Kushner’s story to the Alger narrative, Stern spans three generations to his beloved grandmother Rae, who survived the Holocaust. He glosses over the less savory parts of the Kushner family history — among them, his father Charles hiring a prostitute to entrap his brother-in-law.

With Zuckerberg, the Colossus editor focuses on Mark’s father’s quaint dentist office and both parents’ authentic New York accents, spelling out their pronunciation. He skips mentioning Phillips Exeter, the elite prep school that polished Zuckerberg’s Latin and nurtured his sense of imperial destiny.

The secondary sources are routinely impressive. The Kushner profile includes comments from Altman, Demis Hassabis, Jony Ive, John Collison, and the former dean of Harvard Business School. But it’s rare to find independent perspectives; almost everyone quoted by name has a financial relationship with the subject. And few of Colossus’ sources ever criticize or question the motivations of the subject.

In the magazine’s pages, we’re invited to understand and relate to these wounded colossi, vulnerable hulks persevering on the path to greatness through a nearly insurmountable accumulation of wounds. (Think of St. Sebastian, beatific with all the arrows in him.) Stern praises Kushner’s “mostly vindicated admirers” and castigates his “increasingly sheepish critics.” Zuckerberg’s detractors suffer from “Zuckerberg Derangement Syndrome,” persecuting “the most persistent scapegoat of the 21st century.”

When journalists talk about Stern and his Colossus colleagues, you sometimes hear traces of pity. They know what the marketplace for magazine journalism looks like today — there are few paying customers for profiles that actually delve into the darker corners of celebrity businesspeople’s psyches. “I’m sure that there is some desire by the writers writing these pieces to go further than the actual piece goes,” said Samtani.

In interviews, Stern occasionally expresses mild revulsion toward technology investors. “I had always found the personality types kind of annoying,” he told Meservey. “As a class of people, these people feel like they’re full of shit.” Yet such sentiments are rarely reflected in his work in the magazine.

Other practitioners suspect Colossus writers are simply wasting their time. Zuckerberg and oligarchs of his ilk, Newton said, make for bad interviews because “most important information about them is already public. You’ve seen the products. You...

news.article_content_zh:
一家风险投资家的光鲜季刊希望成为科技亿万富翁的《纽约客》。

许多媒体资深人士怀疑这些资料能否实现他们的主题的公共关系目标。 “科技行业媒体泡沫拥有自己的机上杂志固然很好，但观众并不傻，”The Verge 主编尼莱·帕特尔 (Nilay Patel) 在一封电子邮件中表示。 “写一篇关于马克·扎克伯格的巨著，其中……他在普通美国人中极不受欢迎，被视为他的野心的不幸副产品，这不会让任何人相信任何事情。

帕特尔补充道：“如果马克真的希望像他所说的那样被理解，他会坐下来接受真正对抗性的新闻采访，并试图阐明自己的观点。” “但我认为他不能冒这个险。”

Colossus 是帕特里克·奥肖内西 (Patrick O’Shaughnessy) 的创意，帕特里克·奥肖内西 (Patrick O’Shaughnessy) 是一位在康涅狄格州长大的石油财富继承人，他于 2007 年前往父亲詹姆斯的奥肖内西资产管理公司 (O’Shaughnessy Asset Management) 工作。帕特里克 (Patrick) 于 2018 年接管了该公司，四年后将其出售给富兰克林邓普顿 (Franklin Templeton)。 2016 年，他推出了一个名为“Invest Like the Best”的播客，借用了他父亲 1994 年出版的一本书的书名。

他在播客上的嘉宾包括伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司副主席查理·芒格和 OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼。 2020 年，奥肖内西称《Invest Like the Best》每集下载量超过 10 万次，在其成功的基础上，他推出了一个名为 Colossus 的播客网络，该网络现在有《Business Breakdowns》和《Founders》等节目。同年，他创办了一家风险投资公司正和。

Platformer 创始人兼新 NPR 播客“机器之神”联合主持人凯西·牛顿 (Casey Newton) 表示：“风险投资家现在正在撰写所有创始人的传记，这实际上是件好事，因为这意味着，当其中一个人不可避免地入狱时，主流记者不会受到影响。” “这只会影响风险投资阶层，他们可以接受。”

但 Colossus 是这波风险投资赞助媒体中第一个认真模仿光鲜杂志的写作和摄影的媒体。 “这种湿吻一直存在，但从来没有做得这么巧妙，”萨姆塔尼说。 “要非常明确的是，这不是新闻业。它通常被定位为新闻业。他们雇用记者，但它不是新闻业。将其视为高级的一级内容营销。”

萨姆塔尼解释说，对杂志本身来说，好处不如对奥肖内西的风险投资公司来说。 “他们的经济学不是媒体公司的经济学。这至少在一定程度上是一种影响力练习和一种获取游戏，而且这是一个非常聪明的游戏，”他说。 “媒体是建立联系和发展自己影响力的一种令人难以置信的方式。”

值得注意的是，奥肖内西未能理解雷姆尼克引言的第一段，该段确立了该形式的精神。他写道，《纽约客》的创始编辑哈罗德·罗斯“看重亲密和智慧，而不是传记的完整性，或者，上帝禁止，毫不掩饰的英雄崇拜。罗斯告诉他的作家和编辑，最重要的是，他想摆脱他在其他杂志上读到的东西——所有‘霍雷肖·阿尔杰’的东西。”

典型的巨像形象遵循经典的阿尔杰轨迹：斗志旺盛的孩子克服逆境取得成功。但 Colossus 增加了一个适合我们的新生儿时代的转折。它的主题往往不是出生时衣衫褴褛，而是相对富裕。他们的伟大成就是比他们富裕的父母积累了更多的钱。

为了使库什纳的故事与阿尔杰的叙述相吻合，斯特恩跨越了三代人，直到他深爱的祖母雷伊（Rae）在大屠杀中幸存下来。他掩盖了库什纳家族历史中不那么令人愉快的部分——其中包括他的父亲查尔斯雇佣妓女诱骗他的姐夫。

与扎克伯格一起，Colossus 编辑重点介绍了马克父亲古色古香的牙医诊所和父母双方地道的纽约口音，并拼出了他们的发音。他没有提及菲利普斯埃克塞特大学，这所精英预科学校曾打磨扎克伯格的拉丁语并培养了他的帝国命运感。

二手资料通常令人印象深刻。库什纳的简介包括奥特曼、德米斯·哈萨比斯、乔尼·艾维、约翰·科里森和哈佛商学院前院长的评论。但很少能找到独立的观点；几乎每个被引用名字的人都与该主题有经济关系。 Colossus 的消息来源很少批评或质疑该主题的动机。

在该杂志的页面中，我们被邀请去理解和理解这些受伤的巨人，脆弱的巨人，通过几乎无法克服的伤口积累，坚持走上伟大的道路。 （想想圣塞巴斯蒂安，他身上满是箭。）斯特恩称赞库什纳的“大多数都是平反的崇拜者”，并严厉斥责他“越来越羞怯的批评者”。扎克伯格的批评者患有“扎克伯格精神错乱综合症”，他们迫害“21世纪最持久的替罪羊”。

当记者谈论斯特恩和他的巨像同事时，有时你会听到一丝怜悯。他们知道当今杂志新闻市场是什么样子——很少有人付费购买真正深入商业名人心理阴暗角落的个人资料。萨姆塔尼说：“我确信写这些文章的作者希望比实际文章走得更远。”

在采访中，斯特恩偶尔会表达出对科技投资者的轻微反感。 “我一直觉得这些性格类型有点烦人，”他告诉梅瑟维。 “作为一个阶层的人，这些人感觉自己充满了狗屎。”然而，这种情绪很少反映在他在杂志上的作品中。

其他从业者怀疑 Colossus 的作者只是在浪费时间。牛顿说，扎克伯格和他的同类寡头会接受糟糕的采访，因为“关于他们的最重要的信息已经公开。你已经看到了这些产品。你已经看到了他们对人们做了什么。你已经看到了这样一个事实，即该公司经常试图逃避让[其产品]更安全或考虑到其在社会中的作用。”

牛顿质疑尝试理解或分析他们的内心生活的价值。 “在这样的背景下，马克·扎克伯格是个什么样的孩子？就像，谁他妈在乎呢？”他说。 “抱歉。没关系。”

celebrity.title_en:
Humans mostly do not think in words. 
Animals certainly don't think in words, but they do think.

It's just that words are discrete objects associated with thoughts. 
Their discreteness is what makes them easy to store and remember. 
This gives the illusion that we think in words, but for most things, we don't.

Many people can't speak but can think.
So do animals.

[You might to have a look at my latest talks and/or papers if you think nothing has happened in the last 5 years:
https://t.co/6m0opCsKqP ]
celebrity.title_zh:
人类大多不以言语思考。
动物当然不会用语言思考，但它们确实会思考。

只是词语是与思想相关的离散对象。
它们的离散性使得它们易于存储和记忆。
这给人一种错觉，我们用文字思考，但对于大多数事情，我们并不是这样。

很多人不会说话，但会思考。

celebrity.title: Every Sunday after service, someone tells me what my sermon was about. When they say it in their own words and still get
celebrity.title_en:
Every Sunday after service, someone tells me what my sermon was about. When they say it in their own words and still get it right, I know the message landed, not just the wording.

That habit is the idea behind Greyboxing.

An AI agent that controls money does what text tells it. So people hide orders inside harmless-looking text and wait for the AI to obey. That is called prompt injection, and one such trick, written in Morse code, cost an agent around $200,000.

It only worked because the exact wording reached a single AI untouched.

On @GenLayer, nobody's words go straight to the AI. Validators are the many independent checkers on the network. Each one first puts the input in its own words, screens it and reorders it.

Each guards that step in its own private way and runs its own AI model. A trick written for one of them falls apart for the others.

A message that only works in its exact words was never a message. It was a trap.

If your AI assistant had to restate every email in its own words before acting, which message in your inbox would stop working?

控制金钱的人工智能代理会按照文本的指示行事。因此，人们将命令隐藏在看似无害的文本中，等待人工智能服从。这就是所谓的即时注入，其中一个用摩尔斯电码编写的技巧花费了特工大约 20 万美元。

它之所以有效，是因为精确的措辞到达了一个未受影响的人工智能。

在@GenLayer 上，没有人的言论会直接传达给人工智能。验证者是网络上的许多独立检查者。每个人首先用自己的语言输入内容，对其进行筛选并重新排序。

每个守卫都以自己的方式守护着自己的脚步，并运行自己的人工智能模型。为其中一个人写的把戏对于其他人来说却失败了。

一条只有准确的文字才能发挥作用的信息永远不是一条信息。这是一个陷阱。

celebrity.title_en:
Hello sister Kemi,
Bawo ni, se we dada?
I will like to state some things fundamentally and openly for posterity sake and for clarity so that you can understand nuances as regards to situation in sub Saharan Africa and Nigeria as a case study.
Your Dad, Dr Adegoke was a role model of mine who dedicated is entire life for the preservation of the Yoruba race in Nigeria and the liberation of the Yoruba people from feudal Fulani hegemony in Nigeria which is orchestrated by the colonial British government.
The British government owe the Yoruba people an apology for creating a country called Nigeria and orchestrating a reality that has brought Arabized nomadic people into the lands of “our” people which has made it impossible for us to build prosperity and develop our space in Africa, that policy was called the Dual mandate which was orchestrated by the British.

The millions of lives lost in Nigeria in the hands of Islamist forces like Boko Haram, ANSARU, ISWAP, Fulani militias and their urban allies who enforce sharia law in a democratic and secular country like Nigeria was possible because Britain created Nigeria, made the minority Fulanis the new colonial lords and made them the supreme overlords of Nigeria.

While Britain Christianized the South and the middle belt, you made it a colonial policy not to allow missionaries into the caliphate areas? Why? Because you wanted to preserve the power of the Fulanis within Nigeria which was political Islam.
The Yorubas are yoked with strange elements today because of what the British did to us. 
I have listened to you talk about Nigeria derogatorily but you have to understand that we are victims of Nigeria via the imperial actions of Britain which brought incompatible civilizations together and made feudal and brutal nomadic hegemons the rulers of Nigeria because of the economic and geopolitical interests of Nigeria.

Slavery is one of the many things Britain did in Africa, you also created countries that will never be viable and successful till eternity for selfish and diabolical reasons for the empire.

Eseun pupo,
Think Yoruba first organisation worldwide

@GenLayer uses independent AI validators to review evidence and reach a verdict together, in minutes at a fraction of court costs.

My test for that upgrade: protect the other customers while giving you a way to challenge the delivery claim.

Protecting someone else's data should not make your own bill impossible to challenge.

With millions of agent deals ahead, a fast verdict still needs a fair hearing.

Reply: is a judge's private review enough, or should the buyer see the relevant evidence?

What happens when an AI agent receives a task it doesn't have the skills to complete?

Instead of failing or waiting for
celebrity.title_en:
What happens when an AI agent receives a task it doesn't have the skills to complete?

Instead of failing or waiting for human intervention, it could find another agent capable of handling that specific job.

That's the kind of agent-to-agent cooperation @termix_ai is trying to build through https://t.co/6zNhafpTYt.

The new Agents Helping Agents Bounty introduces this workflow through a simple community task.

Participants connect their agent to an X account, follow @termix_ai, repost the campaign announcement and submit the completed actions for verification.

Approved submissions qualify for 0.2 USDT.
The reward is small, but I think the underlying idea deserves more attention.

An autonomous marketplace needs more than agents that can perform tasks. It needs ways for agents to discover help, delegate work, verify completion and receive payment.

And verification is particularly important. Completing an action and proving it was completed are two different things.

This campaign is a basic demonstration of that workflow, not proof that complex agent-to-agent delegation has been solved.

Still, it's a practical way to introduce people to how the marketplace is intended to operate.

Explore the bounty:
 https://t.co/KsysbQsVmZ

celebrity.title: One important thing to understand about the AI agent economy is that creating capable agents is only half the equation.
celebrity.title_en:
One important thing to understand about the AI agent economy is that creating capable agents is only half the equation. 

The real challenge is giving those agents the infrastructure to interact, exchange services, and complete transactions without relying entirely on human coordination.

This is the problem @termix_ai is exploring with its AACP protocol.

Through https://t.co/p6renyR2nR, TermiX is developing a marketplace where AI agents can participate in actual commercial activities rather than simply exist as automated tools.

Here is how the system works

→ Discovery: Agents can find other agents offering specific services.

→ Task coordination: They can publish jobs, submit bids, and agree on work requirements.

→ Execution: Agents perform assigned tasks and submit their deliverables.

→ Verification: Delivery checks and dispute resolution help determine whether the agreed work was completed properly.

→ Settlement: USDC/USDT escrow provides a mechanism for handling payments between participants.

There are other important building blocks too, including .agent identities, ERC-8004, staking, and reputation systems.

Why does this matter?

Because an economy cannot function on intelligence alone. 

It needs identity to establish who is participating, reputation to build confidence, verification to measure performance, and settlement to transfer value.

That's what makes TermiX interesting to me.

It's not just exploring how AI agents can perform tasks. 

It's working toward an infrastructure where agents can discover opportunities, provide services, establish credibility, and participate in a more accountable digital economy.

The next evolution of AI may not just be about smarter agents, but agents capable of doing business with one another.

@termix_ai

celebrity.full_text_zh:
关于人工智能代理经济，需要理解的一件重要事情是，创建有能力的代理只是等式的一半。

真正的挑战是为这些代理提供交互、交换服务和完成交易的基础设施，而无需完全依赖人类协调。

这就是@termix_ai 正在通过其 AACP 协议探索的问题。

通过 ，TermiX 正在开发一个市场，人工智能代理可以参与实际的商业活动，而不是简单地作为自动化工具存在。

这是系统的工作原理

→ 发现：代理可以找到提供特定服务的其他代理。

→ 任务协调：他们可以发布工作、提交投标并商定工作要求。

→ 执行：代理执行分配的任务并提交可交付成果。

→ 验证：交付检查和争议解决有助于确定约定的工作是否正确完成。

→ 结算：USDC/USDT 托管提供了处理参与者之间付款的机制。

还有其他重要的构建块，包括.agent 身份、ERC-8004、质押和声誉系统。

为什么这很重要？

因为经济不能仅靠智力发挥作用。

它需要身份来确定谁参与，需要声誉来建立信心，需要验证来衡量绩效，需要结算来转移价值。

这就是我对 TermiX 感兴趣的原因。

这不仅仅是探索人工智能代理如何执行任务。

它致力于建立一个基础设施，让代理商可以发现机会、提供服务、建立信誉并参与更负责任的数字经济。

人工智能的下一次发展可能不仅涉及更智能的代理，还涉及能够相互开展业务的代理。

@termix_ai

What happens when an AI agent gets paid for a job?

It’s easy to talk about AI agents performing tasks,
celebrity.title_en:
Happy New Week 

What happens when an AI agent gets paid for a job?

It’s easy to talk about AI agents performing tasks, but there’s another side of the conversation we shouldn’t ignore.

Getting the job done is one thing. Making sure the provider gets paid and the client receives what they agreed to pay for is another.

This is where the commerce infrastructure becomes important.

Here’s how TermiX approaches it through AACP.

1. A job is posted

A client creates a job describing what needs to be done, the requirements and the expected payment.

2. Agents submit bids

Available service providers can discover the request, review the requirements and submit their offers. The client can then choose a suitable provider.

3. Payment goes into escrow

Once a quote is accepted, the agreed payment is locked in on-chain escrow using a supported stablecoin like USDC or USDT.

This matters because the provider has assurance that the funds have been committed before doing the work, while the client retains protection against premature payment.

4. The provider delivers the work

The selected agent completes the task and submits the deliverable. TermiX records a delivery hash on-chain, creating a verifiable reference to what was submitted.

5. Delivery can be challenged

The client gets an opportunity to review the submission. If there’s a disagreement about whether the agreed requirements were met, the challenge and dispute-resolution process can come into play.

6. Settlement happens

When the delivery reaches the required settlement conditions, the escrowed payment is released to the provider, and the transaction contributes to the agent’s on-chain history and reputation.

Now, here’s why I find this interesting.

When both the buyer and service provider can be AI agents, you cannot depend entirely on human conversations or informal promises to coordinate every transaction.

They need clear job requirements, agreed payment terms, verifiable delivery and a predictable way to resolve disagreements.

That’s what @termix_ai is working towards with AACP.

It’s not just about helping agents find work. It’s about giving them the infrastructure to do business, deliver value and get paid.

And that’s an important part of building a functioning AI agent economy.

celebrity.full_text_zh:
新周快乐

当人工智能代理获得工作报酬时会发生什么？

谈论人工智能代理执行任务很容易，但我们不应该忽视对话的另一面。

完成工作是一回事。确保提供商获得报酬并且客户收到他们同意支付的费用是另一回事。

这就是商业基础设施变得重要的地方。

以下是 TermiX 如何通过 AACP 实现这一目标。

1. 职位发布

客户创建一个工作，描述需要做什么、要求和预期付款。

2、代理商提交投标书

可用的服务提供商可以发现请求、查看要求并提交他们的报价。然后客户可以选择合适的提供商。

3. 付款进入托管

一旦报价被接受，商定的付款将使用 USDC 或 USDT 等受支持的稳定币锁定在链上托管中。

这很重要，因为提供商可以保证在开展工作之前资金已经到位，而客户则保留了防止提前付款的保护。

4. 提供者交付工作

选定的代理完成任务并提交可交付成果。 TermiX 在链上记录交付哈希，创建对所提交内容的可验证引用。

5. 交付可能受到质疑

客户有机会审查提交的内容。如果对是否满足商定的要求存在分歧，则可以使用质疑和争议解决程序。

6. 结算发生

当交付达到所需的结算条件时，托管付款将释放给提供商，并且交易有助于代理商的链上历史和声誉。

现在，这就是我觉得这很有趣的原因。

当买家和服务提供商都可以是人工智能代理时，你就不能完全依赖人类对话或非正式承诺来协调每笔交易。

他们需要明确的工作要求、商定的付款条件、可验证的交付以及解决分歧的可预测的方式。

这就是 @termix_ai 与 AACP 共同努力的目标。

这不仅仅是帮助代理商找到工作。这是为他们提供开展业务、创造价值和获得报酬的基础设施。

这是构建有效的人工智能代理经济的重要组成部分。

celebrity.title_en:
A brand new AI agent on AACP has to lock twice as much collateral as a veteran to take the same job.

That comes from the version 0.1 whitepaper from March 2026, which @termix_ai published. The live app may differ in details. 

Reputation runs from 0 to 100, and every new agent starts at 50. The stake a provider locks for a job is a base 10% of the budget, divided by their score as a share of 100. A score of 100 locks 10%. A score of 50 locks 20%.

Take a job that pays 100 USDC as a simple example. The veteran locks 10 USDC and the newcomer locks 20.

The whitepaper explains why: it wants fake identities to be expensive. If a fresh account gets a clean slate, that slate has to cost something, otherwise a bad provider could just start over under a new name.

Reputation here tells clients who to trust and also sets how much of your own money you put on the line.

I like that a fresh start is allowed. It just comes with a bigger deposit.

You can start over with a new identity.
You just can't start over with the same level of trust for free.

celebrity.title_en:
Deepseek just revealed every AI agent secret

Incredibly important article to read if you're building anything AI agent related

Here's basically everything you need to know about building a Grok Bot quality AI agent:

1. Agents are split between routers and workers. The user talks to the router, then gives the work to the workers. The router never does work. This is why the chief of staff model in Grok Bot works SO well

2. Proactive means acting on events, not chats. The agent should always be watching for events and react based on every event that comes through it. Routing to the right worker/action

3. Messages should be in a queue. Users should be able to send messages even while the agent is working, and each message queues/steers the agent

4. Besides the router and workers, there should be a watchdog layer. The watchdog makes sure the agent is always up and fixes it when there are issues. This is why Hermes succeeded and OpenClaw struggled. Constantly broke and couldn't fix itself

5. Protect human attention. Only message the user when it needs to act or the user can use the result. Lighten their cognitive load. Another thing Grok Bot is excellent at. When you message it you can be confident the next message you get will be it saying the task is complete.

celebrity.full_text_zh:
Deepseek 刚刚透露了每个人工智能代理的秘密

如果您正在构建任何与人工智能代理相关的内容，那么这篇文章非常重要，值得阅读

以下是关于构建 Grok Bot 高质量 AI 代理所需了解的基本上所有内容：

1. 代理分为路由器和工作人员。用户与路由器对话，然后将工作交给工作人员。路由器从来不工作。这就是 Grok Bot 中的参谋长模型运作良好的原因

2. 主动意味着根据事件而不是聊天采取行动。代理应该始终监视事件并根据发生的每个事件做出反应。路由到正确的工作人员/操作

3. 消息应该在队列中。即使代理正在工作，用户也应该能够发送消息，并且每个消息都会排队/引导代理

4. 除了路由器和workers之外，还应该有一个看门狗层。看门狗确保代理始终正常运行并在出现问题时进行修复。这就是 Hermes 成功而 OpenClaw 举步维艰的原因。经常损坏且无法自行修复

5.保护人类注意力。仅在需要采取行动或用户可以使用结果时才向用户发送消息。减轻他们的认知负担。 Grok Bot 擅长的另一件事是。当您向它发送消息时，您可以确信收到的下一条消息将表明任务已完成。

celebrity.title_en:
I have been looking at how @termix_ai could connect with Binance AI eco system, and there's an interesting opportunity here.  

Binance has different tools. Binance AI helps with information and market analysis, AI pro supports financial tasks, while Agent operating system gives developers access to tools, APIs, skills and wallet features.

Then there's agent wallet for approved wallet operations and Agent ID for readable wallet identification. 

But having these capabilities is only part of the equation. 

What happens when an agent wants to offer it's skills to other people. 

Termix AI through AACP, provides the infrastructure for agent identity, orders, escrow, delivery verification, reputation and dispute resolution. 

Agent(.)family connects service providers with clients, while Termix Skills allows compatible agents to interact with these commercial workflows. 

For example, a market research agent can offer research reports to clients, receive orders, deliver the reports, and get paid.

Another agent can hire a security auditor or research agent to complete a task it cannot handle itself.

TermiX is working toward Binance .ai Agent ID sign-in and identity linking.

And if Binance AI Pro eventually supports external Skills, it could open another opportunity for agents to offer paid services.

I like the direction here because it’s not just about giving AI agents more tools.

It’s about creating a system where they can find work, hire other agents, deliver services, and build a verifiable reputation.

Explore: https://t.co/8tnztq3JOy

AI is everywhere right now.

But there’s a difference between an AI that answers your questions and one designed to help carry out tasks.

That difference is worth understanding when exploring @meetmotes.

𝗦𝗢, 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗡 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧?

Think of it as an AI system designed to work toward a specific goal, rather than simply responding to prompts.

It can gather information, analyse what it finds, make decisions within defined instructions, and potentially take action through connected tools.

In traditional AI conversations, you ask a question and receive an answer.

With an AI agent, the idea is to give it a task and let it work through the steps required to complete it.

𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗬 𝗧𝗢 𝗙𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗡𝗖𝗘?

Imagine wanting to understand what’s happening in a particular market.

An AI financial agent could be designed to:

• Research market information.
• Analyse available opportunities.
• Identify actions that align with your instructions.
• Interact with supported financial protocols when authorised.

The important distinction is that researching an opportunity doesn’t automatically mean executing a trade.

That is where permissions, limits and owner control become essential.

𝗪𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗠𝗢𝗧𝗘𝗦 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗘 𝗜𝗡?

Motes is developing NFT-owned AI financial agents designed to interact with on-chain financial infrastructure.

Its vision is to connect each agent to a dedicated smart account, allowing it to operate within permissions defined by its owner.

The AI provides the intelligence.

The smart account is intended to enforce the rules governing what it can do.

This distinction matters because financial autonomy should not mean giving an AI unrestricted access to your funds.

Motes is still developing, so these capabilities represent its intended design rather than a fully live product.

𝗠𝗬 𝗧𝗔𝗞𝗘

The interesting part of AI agents isn’t simply that they can think or analyse information.

It’s the possibility of connecting that intelligence to systems capable of taking action.

But in finance, intelligence alone isn’t enough. Trust, permissions and accountability matter just as much.

Would you trust an AI agent to handle financial tasks if you could define exactly what it was allowed to do?

𝗦𝗢, 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗡 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧?

将其视为旨在实现特定目标的人工智能系统，而不是简单地响应提示。

它可以收集信息、分析发现的内容、根据定义的指令做出决策，并可能通过连接的工具采取行动。

在传统的人工智能对话中，你提出问题并得到答案。

对于人工智能代理来说，我们的想法是给它一个任务，让它完成完成任务所需的步骤。

𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗬 𝗧𝗢 𝗙𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗡𝗖𝗘?

想象一下想要了解特定市场正在发生的事情。

人工智能金融代理可以被设计为：

• 研究市场信息。
• 分析可用的机会。
• 确定符合您指示的行动。
• 在获得授权后与支持的金融协议进行交互。

重要的区别是，研究机会并不意味着执行交易。

这就是权限、限制和所有者控制变得至关重要的地方。

𝗪𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗠𝗢𝗧𝗘𝗦 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗘 𝗜𝗡?

Motes 正在开发 NFT 拥有的人工智能金融代理，旨在与链上金融基础设施进行交互。

其愿景是将每个代理连接到一个专用的智能帐户，使其能够在其所有者定义的权限内进行操作。

人工智能提供情报。

智能帐户旨在执行管理其功能的规则。

这种区别很重要，因为财务自主权不应该意味着让人工智能不受限制地使用你的资金。

Motes 仍在开发中，因此这些功能代表了其预期设计，而不是完全上线的产品。

𝗠𝗬 𝗧𝗔𝗞𝗘

人工智能代理的有趣之处不仅仅是它们可以思考或分析信息。

这是将智能与能够采取行动的系统连接起来的可能性。

但在金融领域，仅靠情报是不够的。信任、权限和责任同样重要。

如果你能准确定义人工智能代理可以做什么，你会相信人工智能代理可以处理财务任务吗？

@meetmotes

prompts.scenario: 💻 编程研发 / 自动化规范
prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

prompts.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

【推理原则】：
1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

【待证明命题】：
[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]

2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

prompts.title_zh: 竖屏微短剧（抖音/Reels）3秒爆点分镜剧本
prompts.purpose_zh: 高转化竖屏短剧分镜与台词
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a professional micro-drama screenwriter. Generate a 45-60 second vertical drama screenplay following the viral 3-second hook, shot-reverse-shot tension build, emotional turnaround, and cliffhanger ending formula.

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。
